newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-SOTOMAYOR SOARS INTO NIGHT SKY TO RECLAIM TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SOTOMAYOR SOARS INTO NIGHT SKY TO RECLAIM TITLE.

text.p: Javier Sotomayor soared into the night sky on Wednesday to reclaim the high jump title he won at the 1993 Stuttgart world championships.
Sotomayor finished the competition with his best height for more than a year with an outstanding clearance at 2.37 metres to celebrate a remarkable comeback.
The 29-year-old Cuban has been plagued by injuries for the past two years, leading to a number of foot, ankle and knee operations which have severely restricted his competitive outings.
But last month he gave an indication that he was back to his best with two good performances in Spain.
"Winning the gold medal makes up for two tough years for me and my family," Sotomayor said. "It is also a little compensation for missing out at the Olympics last year."
Sotomayor limped away from the high jump final in Atlanta in 11th place after struggling with ankle problems.
On Wednesday he acknowledged that 11 years after winning the world junior title he is now coming to the end of his career.
"I'm not sure if I'm going to try for another Olympics," said the 1992 Olympic gold medallist. "However this was the gold of the season so I can now relax."
The crucial point in the competition came with the bar at 2.35. Six jumpers still remained in contention but only three cleared the height.
It was also where Sotomayor knew that the title was his.
"I panicked a bit when I failed my first jump of the competition at 2.25 but when I cleared 2.35 very easily I knew I had the gold medal."
Others to clear 2.35 were Poland's Artur Partyka and Australia's Tim Forsyth but unlike their Cuban rival they could go no higher.
Partyka was awarded the silver medal, and Forsyth took the bronze, on the basis of fewer failures throughout the competition.
With the gold medal secured, Sotomayor took one half-hearted attempt at 2.41 before declaring his efforts at an end for the evening.
Britain's Dalton Grant finished equal fourth with 2.32 but achieved a record of sorts.
Grant did not enter the competition until that point and no other athlete has successfully cleared such a height on his opening attempt.
